column2: follow-up question (asked when this keyPoint is uncertain; must not contain the answer)
Compare the eye with a photographic device: which parts do the jobs of the lens and of the screen, and where does the first bending of light happen?
Describe the journey from the light entering the eye in a dim room to you understanding what you see.
You look up from a book to a distant tree. What changes in the lens of your eye, and what do the muscles do?
Hold this page closer and closer to your eyes. What happens and what is the closest distance at which a normal eye reads comfortably?
A student in the last row cannot read the board but reads a book easily. Where is the image of the board forming in their eye?
What kind of spectacle lens would help someone whose eye focuses the picture too soon, and how does it help?
An older relative holds the newspaper at arm's length to read but sees faraway signs fine. Where does the picture of the paper form in their eye?
Which kind of lens adds the focussing power that is missing, and what two physical reasons can cause the shortage?
Why do many people need reading glasses as they get older even if their eyesight was perfect when young?
How can one pair of spectacles help a person who cannot see far and cannot see near?
What is it about the shape of a prism's faces that makes it different from a rectangular block of glass?
Follow a ray through a glass prism, saying how it bends at each surface and how the final direction compares with the starting direction.
Why does the same beam of white light come out of a prism as a fan of separate colours rather than as a single white beam?
What did Newton do to show that the prism did not create the colours but only separated them?
Explain what a single raindrop does to a ray of sunlight from the moment it enters to the moment it leaves.
To see a rainbow, which way should you face compared with where the Sun is?
Why does the light from a distant star not arrive along a perfectly steady path?
What is it about the size of what we see in the sky that makes one steady and the other flicker?
By how much does the day appear to be lengthened at each end, and what is responsible?
Why does the setting Sun look slightly squashed instead of perfectly round?
Why can you see a beam of sunlight coming through a small hole in a smoky room, but not in perfectly clean air?
If the scattering particles in the air get much bigger, how would the colour of the light thrown sideways change?
Sunlight contains all the colours. Why does the clear daytime sky nevertheless look blue?
What would an astronaut see in the sky and why, and why do traffic danger lights use red?
